capture.final_message:
Split the conjunction and use the natural multiplicative decompositions in each part.

- For the cardinal statement, \(\aleph_0 \le a\) makes \(a\) infinite, so cardinal arithmetic gives
  \[
  a\cdot a=a.
  \]
  The only multiplicative unit cardinal is \(1\), while an infinite \(a\) is not a unit. Thus this expresses \(a\) as a product of two nonunits, contradicting irreducibility.

- For the arithmetic-function statement, the forward implication follows immediately by evaluating \(f=g\) at \(p^i\). Conversely, prove equality by extensionality on \(n:\mathbb N\). At \(n=0\), arithmetic functions vanish by definition; at \(n=1\), multiplicativity gives the normalized value \(1\). For \(n>1\), use unique prime factorization
  \[
  n=\prod_p p^{v_p(n)}.
  \]
  Distinct prime-power factors are coprime, so repeated application of multiplicativity reconstructs \(f(n)\) and \(g(n)\) as the corresponding finite products. The assumed equality on every prime power then makes these products equal.

The key point is that no additive or cancellation structure on \(R\) is needed: a commutative monoid with zero supplies exactly the multiplication, unit, and zero values used in this reconstruction.
